provenance.note: every value is deterministic: none of these builders derives a key, and the credential, issuer, registry, and timestamp are the pinned `test-utils.ts` mock credential's own, which the credential builder reproduces byte for byte

declarations.issuance_saidify_expression: Saider.saidify({ v: versify(Protocols.KERI, undefined, Serials.JSON, 0), t: Ilks.iss, d: '', i: acdc.d, s: '0', ri: args.ri, dt: subject.dt, })
declarations.issuance_anchor_expression: interact({ pre: hab.prefix, sn: sn + 1, data: [ { i: iss.i, s: iss.s, d: iss.d, }, ], dig: hab.state.d, version: undefined, kind: undefined, })
declarations.revocation_literal: _rev = { v: vs, t: Ilks.rev, d: '', i: said, s: '1', ri: registryId, p: cred.status.d, dt: dt, }
declarations.revocation_anchor_expression: interact({ pre: pre, sn: sn + 1, data: data, dig: dig, version: undefined, kind: undefined, })
declarations.revocation_registry_fallback: if ('ri' in cred.sad && cred.sad.ri !== undefined) { registryId = cred.sad.ri; } else if ('rd' in cred.sad && cred.sad.rd !== undefined) { registryId = cred.sad.rd; } else { throw new Error('Neither ri nor rd property found in credential'); }
declarations.acdc_attachment_body: export function serializeACDCAttachment(anc: Serder): Uint8Array { const prefixer = new Prefixer({ qb64: anc.pre }); const seqner = new Seqner({ sn: anc.sn }); const saider = new Saider({ qb64: anc.sad['d'] }); const craw = new Uint8Array(); const ctr = new Counter({ code: CtrDex.SealSourceTriples, count: 1 }).qb64b; const prefix = prefixer.qb64b; const seq = seqner.qb64b; const said = saider.qb64b; const newCraw = new Uint8Array( craw.length + ctr.length + prefix.length + seq.length + said.length ); newCraw.set(craw); newCraw.set(ctr, craw.length); newCraw.set(prefix, craw.length + ctr.length); newCraw.set(seq, craw.length + ctr.length + prefix.length); newCraw.set(said, craw.length + ctr.length + prefix.length + seq.length); return newCraw; }
declarations.iss_attachment_body: export function serializeIssExnAttachment(anc: Serder): Uint8Array { const seqner = new Seqner({ sn: anc.sn }); const ancSaider = new Saider({ qb64: anc.sad['d'] }); const coupleArray = new Uint8Array( seqner.qb64b.length + ancSaider.qb64b.length ); coupleArray.set(seqner.qb64b); coupleArray.set(ancSaider.qb64b, seqner.qb64b.length); const counter = new Counter({ code: CtrDex.SealSourceCouples, count: 1, }); const counterQb64b = counter.qb64b; const atc = new Uint8Array(counter.qb64b.length + coupleArray.length); atc.set(counterQb64b); atc.set(coupleArray, counterQb64b.length); if (atc.length % 4 !== 0) { throw new Error( `Invalid attachments size: ${atc.length}, non-integral quadlets detected.` ); } const pcnt = new Counter({ code: CtrDex.AttachedMaterialQuadlets, count: Math.floor(atc.length / 4), }); const msg = new Uint8Array(pcnt.qb64b.length + atc.length); msg.set(pcnt.qb64b); msg.set(atc, pcnt.qb64b.length); return msg; }

notes.issuance: the `iss` event's `dt` is the credential's *attribute* timestamp — `dt: subject.dt` — not a second clock reading, so issuing commits the credential and its transaction event to the same instant
notes.issuance_anchor: the anchoring interaction seals one `{i, s, d}` triple naming the transaction event, at the issuer's next sequence number, over the key state's digest
notes.revocation: the `rev` event's sequence number is the literal string '1' and its `p` is the credential's current status digest, so the reference can only revoke a credential whose transaction log holds exactly one prior event
notes.attachments: `serializeACDCAttachment` is passed the *issuance* event despite its parameter being named `anc`, so the triple names (credential SAID, 0, iss SAID); `serializeIssExnAttachment` is passed the anchor and produces a pipelined couple naming it

pinned_mock_credential.note: the issuance of the credential the pinned `test-utils.ts` checks in, at the issuer's first interaction; its `iss` SAID is the one `credentialing.test.ts` publishes

later_in_the_log.note: an issuance anchored well into the issuer's key event log

hexadecimal_sequence_number.note: an anchor whose sequence number needs hexadecimal digits, which the event writes lowercase and unpadded

large_sequence_number.note: an anchor at a sequence number past 32 bits

distinct_timestamp.note: a credential stamped at a different instant, which changes the transaction event alone

pinned_mock_credential.note: revoking the pinned mock credential, whose prior transaction event is the issuance above

later_in_the_log.note: a revocation anchored well into the issuer's key event log

distinct_timestamp.note: a revocation at a different instant

pinned_artifacts.note: the pinned `credentialing.test.ts` builds an `iss` and an `ixn` by hand and asserts the IPEX grant embedding them; rebuilding both from the reference's own expressions reproduces the published `iss` SAID, and both attachment strings appear verbatim inside the published grant attachment

pinned_serializers.note: `test/core/utils.test.ts` asserts both serializers directly; its `iss` case carries no `s` field at all, so `Serder.sn` reads it as zero

revocation_sequence_number_is_always_one.note: `_rev.s` is the literal string '1', so the reference can only revoke a credential whose transaction log holds exactly one prior event. A credential in a backed registry, whose log carries backer rotations, or one somehow revoked twice, gets an event claiming a position it does not occupy.
revocation_sequence_number_is_always_one.rust_decision: the sequence number is a required input, defaulting to one; the reference's only reachable value is reproduced and anything else is expressible.

revocation_reads_the_registry_from_ri_or.fallback_expression: if ('ri' in cred.sad && cred.sad.ri !== undefined) { registryId = cred.sad.ri; } else if ('rd' in cred.sad && cred.sad.rd !== undefined) { registryId = cred.sad.rd; } else { throw new Error('Neither ri nor rd property found in credential'); }
revocation_reads_the_registry_from_ri_or.note: revocation accepts the KERI 2 spelling `rd` as well as `ri`, and throws when neither is present — but the credential builder always writes `ri`, so the `rd` branch is unreachable from a credential this port built.
revocation_reads_the_registry_from_ri_or.rust_decision: the registry is a typed required input; `rd` is unrepresentable here, as CESR 2 is out of scope.

revocation_timestamp_defaults_to_the_clo.note: the revocation timestamp defaults to a clock reading with three zero digits standing in for microseconds it never had, exactly as the credential's attribute timestamp does.
revocation_timestamp_defaults_to_the_clo.rust_decision: required: a protocol crate reads no clock, so the timestamp is a validated `Timestamp` the caller supplies.

issuance_reuses_the_credential_timestamp.note: the `iss` event takes `dt: subject.dt` — the credential's own attribute timestamp — rather than reading the clock a second time, so a credential and its transaction event always agree.
issuance_reuses_the_credential_timestamp.rust_decision: reproduced, and made structural: the issuance builder reads the timestamp off the credential rather than taking one.

acdc_attachment_is_passed_the_issuance_e.note: `serializeACDCAttachment(anc)` names its parameter `anc` but every call site passes the *issuance* event, so the triple it builds is (credential SAID, 0, iss SAID) — the credential's own transaction inception, not the key event anchoring it.
acdc_attachment_is_passed_the_issuance_e.rust_decision: the attachment is a method on the issuance event, so there is no parameter to pass the wrong value to.

missing_sequence_number_reads_as_zero.note: `Serder.sn` builds a `CesrNumber` from `sad['s']`; the pinned `utils.test.ts` vector has no `s` field at all, and the resulting couple carries sequence number zero rather than failing.
missing_sequence_number_reads_as_zero.rust_decision: unrepresentable: a sequence number is a `u128` on the typed event, never read back out of an untyped map.

establishment_only_is_unimplemented.note: both `issue` and `revoke` throw outright when the issuer's configuration carries the `EO` trait, because anchoring in an establishment-only log needs a rotation event neither builds.
establishment_only_is_unimplemented.rust_decision: the anchor is an interaction event and nothing else; an establishment-only issuer is refused with a typed error naming the trait, rather than throwing a string.

backed_transaction_events_have_no_builde.note: the ilk table declares `bis` and `brv` — the backed spellings of issuance and revocation, used when a registry has backers — but nothing in the pinned tree constructs either.
backed_transaction_events_have_no_builde.rust_decision: `N/A`, on the same evidence as keri-protocol's receipt and query messages; the ilks exist in `keri-protocol::event::kind` and no builder is invented here.

revocation_prior_comes_from_the_server.note: `p` is read from `cred.status.d`, the credential state KERIA returns, so the reference cannot revoke without first fetching the credential.
revocation_prior_comes_from_the_server.rust_decision: the prior digest is a required typed input, so revocation artifacts are constructible offline from a status a caller already holds.
